codeartifactRepoPolicyBroad.^description: {$COUNT} CodeArtifact domain(s) or repository(ies) have a resource policy with an Allow statement for any principal ("*") that is not scoped by an aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalAccount or similar condition. Depending on the actions granted, any AWS account can read packages from, or publish packages to, your private registry, which exposes internal code and opens a supply-chain injection path into every build that consumes it.
codeartifactRepoPolicyBroad.shortDesc: Scope CodeArtifact resource policies to your organization

codeartifactNotUsed.^description: {$COUNT} region(s) have no AWS CodeArtifact domain or repository. A private package registry gives builds a single curated, access-controlled source for third-party and internal dependencies, with package origin controls against dependency substitution. Without one, builds commonly fetch packages directly from public registries. This is a weak signal: another private registry or a different Region may already provide this control, so review before acting.
codeartifactNotUsed.shortDesc: Use a private package registry such as CodeArtifact

codeartifactPackageOriginUnrestricted.^description: {$COUNT} CodeArtifact repository(ies) contain packages whose origin controls allow BOTH direct publishing and ingestion from upstream sources, while the repository can reach a public registry through an external connection. For an internal package this permits dependency substitution: a same-named version published to the public registry can be pulled in and mixed with your internal versions. Internal packages should set upstream to BLOCK; packages consumed from public registries should set publish to BLOCK.
codeartifactPackageOriginUnrestricted.shortDesc: Restrict package origin controls on internal packages
